log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Dragapult + Rotom-Wash lead: Dragapult outspeeds everything, threatens Mega Gengar with Life Orb Shadow Ball (85–167% roll), and is Ghost-immune to Shadow Tag. Rotom-Wash walls Excadrill completely (Levitate + resistances), 2HKOs Tyranitar with Hydro Pump, and Volt Switches out of trapping. Klefki in back sets Prankster Light Clay screens to blunt sand-boosted Rock Slides and Thunder Waves Gengar to neutralise its speed. Incineroar cycles Intimidate + Fake Out with Chople Berry to eat Tauros-Aqua Close Combat. Corviknight and Metagross sit out; screens + Intimidate cycling better handles the sand-and-trapping matchup.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Dragapult + Rotom-Wash, back Klefki + Incineroar. Dragapult immune to Shadow Tag, threatens Gengar. Rotom-Wash walls Excadrill, threatens Tyranitar. Klefki sets screens and T-waves Gengar. Incineroar Intimidate cycles.

decisions.rationale: Lead the sand core: Tyranitar's Sand Stream triggers on entry, immediately boosting Excadrill to 280 Spe — outspeeding the entire opponent's team including max-Speed Dragapult (213). Rock Slide spread + Focus Sash insurance makes this the safest, most reliable lead. Back: Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost foes like Klefki/Incineroar/Rotom-W/Metagross/Corviknight for late-game elimination, Taunt shuts screens/status, Energy Ball hits Rotom-W SE) and Houndoom (Flamethrower OHKOs Klefki and threatens Metagross-Mega/Corviknight, Dark Pulse OHKOs Dragapult, Flash Fire absorbs Incineroar Fire moves). This covers all six opponent Pokémon across the four brought.
decisions.notebook: Rematch vs deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (won 2-0 week 4 with same six). Opponent knows sand core. Gengar-Mega max Spe = 200 (Timid/32), loses to max-Speed Dragapult (213) — Excadrill under sand (280) is the only reliable speed control. Excadrill moves all neutral into Dragapult but outspeeds. Metagross-Mega and Corviknight both heavily walled by Excadrill (Steel/Psychic and Flying/Steel doubly NVE or immune into Ground/Steel). Rotom-W Levitate dodges Ground; Gengar Energy Ball is the SE answer. Klefki Prankster screens outspeed Gengar Taunt T1 but Shadow Tag traps it for T2 Taunt. Houndoom Dark Pulse OHKOs Dragapult, Flamethrower OHKOs Klefki. Plan: sand lead, wear down with Rock Slide spread, bring Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag trapping and Houndoom for targeted wallbreaking. Watch for opponent anti-leading Rotom-W + Klefki to burn/screen.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult is threatened by a likely double-target from Excadrill Iron Head (49–70%) + Tyranitar Crunch (91–127%), which together guarantee a KO before Dragapult can move. Protect at +4 priority negates both attacks safely. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump into Tyranitar deals 42–75% (2× super effective), applying immediate pressure while Rotom-Wash comfortably tanks anything the opponent throws at it (Excadrill Iron Head does 10–13%, Crunch 35–50%). This preserves Dragapult — my fastest mon and best answer to a potential Mega Gengar — and sets up a strong turn 2 where Dragapult can Fire Blast Excadrill to break its Sash.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Dragapult + Rotom-Wash, back Klefki + Incineroar. Opponent leads Tyranitar + Excadrill. Sand Rush Excadrill outspeeds Dragapult. Rotom-Wash walls Excadrill (Levitate immune to High Horsepower, 4× resist Iron Head). Dragapult is the primary target; Protect turn 1 to scout and preserve. Klefki sets screens later; Incineroar provides Intimidate cycling.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill (280 Spe, guaranteed first) opens Rock Slide hitting both foes for ~17-34% each with 30% flinch on Dragapult and Rotom-W. Tyranitar follows with Crunch on Dragapult (SE 2x, 56-108%). Combined ~79-148% + sand chip very likely KOs Dragapult, removing the faster threat. If Dragapult Protects, Rock Slide still chips Rotom-W. If Rock Slide flinches Dragapult, it can't Protect or attack, and Crunch lands clean. Excadrill Focus Sash covers Fire Blast (81-122%). Tyranitar survives Hydro Pump (36-55%). Best opening to eliminate the speed threat while guaranteeing chip on Rotom-W.
decisions.notebook: Rematch vs deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (won 2-0 week 4 with same six). Opponent knows sand core. Gengar-Mega max Spe = 200 (Timid/32), loses to max-Speed Dragapult (213) — Excadrill under sand (280) is the only reliable speed control. Metagross-Mega and Corviknight both heavily walled by Excadrill (Steel/Psychic and Flying/Steel doubly NVE or immune into Ground/Steel). Rotom-W Levitate dodges Ground; Gengar Energy Ball is the SE answer. Klefki Prankster screens outspeed Gengar Taunt T1 but Shadow Tag traps it for T2 Taunt. Houndoom Dark Pulse OHKOs Dragapult, Flamethrower OHKOs Klefki. Plan: sand lead, wear down with Rock Slide spread, bring Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag trapping and Houndoom for targeted wallbreaking. Watch for opponent anti-leading Rotom-W + Klefki to burn/screen. Key T1 damage: TTar Crunch on Dragapult 56-108% (SE), Excadrill Rock Slide spread 17-34% each, combined likely KOs Dragapult. Dragapult Fire Blast 81-122% on Excadrill (sash saves). Rotom-W Hydro Pump 36-55% on TTar (survives).

decisions.rationale: Switch Dragapult to Incineroar for Intimidate (-1 Atk on both foes) while Rotom-Wash burns Tyranitar. This double-dips on Tyranitar's Attack (Intimidate + burn = 0.25x), neutralizing their primary Dragapult answer. Incineroar resists Iron Head and Crunch, taking only ~17-25% and ~16-22% respectively. The main risk is Excadrill predicting the switch with High Horsepower (83-117% into Incineroar), but Iron Head is the more standard play into Dragapult. Even in the worst case, Dragapult is preserved in the back and a burned Tyranitar is crippled for the rest of the game.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult + Rotom-Wash lead vs Tyranitar + Excadrill. Turn 1: Dragapult Protected, Rotom-Wash flinched by Rock Slide. Turn 2: Switched Dragapult to Incineroar for Intimidate, Rotom-Wash Will-O-Wisp on Tyranitar. Klefki in back for screens later. Excadrill has Focus Sash; Rotom-Wash walls it with Levitate. Tyranitar's Crunch threatens Dragapult with OHKO range.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill Protects to preserve Focus Sash and avoid the double-target KO (Dragapult Fire Blast breaks sash, Rotom Hydro Pump guaranteed OHKO after). Tyranitar Crunch is SE on Dragapult (56-108% from 93% HP) — likely KO or leaves it at very low HP for easy cleanup. Even if opponent predicts Protect and pivots to Tyranitar, Thunderbolt is only 11-17% and Hydro Pump 36-55%, so Tyranitar survives comfortably. This preserves our only speed control (Excadrill 280 under sand) while removing the opponent's fastest threat.
decisions.notebook: Rematch vs deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (won 2-0 week 4 with same six). Opponent knows sand core. Gengar-Mega max Spe = 200 (Timid/32), loses to max-Speed Dragapult (213) — Excadrill under sand (280) is the only reliable speed control. Metagross-Mega and Corviknight both heavily walled by Excadrill (Steel/Psychic and Flying/Steel doubly NVE or immune into Ground/Steel). Rotom-W Levitate dodges Ground; Gengar Energy Ball is the SE answer. Klefki Prankster screens outspeed Gengar Taunt T1 but Shadow Tag traps it for T2 Taunt. Houndoom Dark Pulse OHKOs Dragapult, Flamethrower OHKOs Klefki. Plan: sand lead, wear down with Rock Slide spread, bring Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag trapping and Houndoom for targeted wallbreaking. T2 confirmed: Dragapult Thunderbolt on TTar only 11-17% (TTar very safe). Dragapult Protect used T1 — reduced success rate makes re-Protect unlikely. Opponent likely double-targets Excadrill to break sash + KO with Rotom Hydro Pump.

decisions.rationale: Reflect goes first (Prankster +1) and halves physical damage for 8 turns with Light Clay, letting Klefki survive Excadrill's High Horsepower barring a Helping Hand + high roll. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump into Excadrill breaks Focus Sash or OHKOs, removing the Sand Rush sweeper's integrity. Even if Klefki falls to a Helping Hand + High Horsepower high roll, Reflect remains and Excadrill is left at 1 HP, easily cleaned next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, burned) + Excadrill (Focus Sash, Sand Rush) and two of Gengar-Mega, Houndoom, Gholdengo, Tauros-Aqua. Rotom-Wash walls Excadrill with Levitate. Klefki's Prankster fails against Dark-type targets (Tyranitar); Thunder Wave also fails vs Ground (Excadrill). Burn on Tyranitar cuts its physical damage. Excadrill's Protect success rate is reduced after turn 2 use.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill High Horsepower is a guaranteed OHKO on Klefki (129–242% even unboosted, and Klefki is at 92% with Def -1), removing the Prankster Thunder Wave / screens threat permanently. Klefki's Prankster Thunder Wave (priority +1) may still fire before Excadrill attacks, but paralysis doesn't prevent the move this turn, so the KO lands regardless. Tyranitar Protects because it's burned (physical damage halved), slower than Rotom (81 vs 106–138, so Rock Slide can't flinch), and Hydro Pump does 35.7–55.1% to Tyranitar — Protect preserves HP for later sand/Intimidate walling. If Rotom redirects Hydro Pump to Excadrill, Focus Sash saves it at 1 HP and we can pivot next turn. Rock Slide chip from burned Tyranitar is only 9.6–18.4% on Rotom, not worth eating a Hydro Pump.
decisions.notebook: Excadrill High Horsepower guaranteed OHKOs Klefki at 92% + Def -1 (129–242%); Helping Hand unnecessary. Rotom Hydro Pump OHKOs Excadrill through sash range (109–158%) and does 35.7–55.1% to Tyranitar. Burned Tyranitar Rock Slide chip on Rotom is only 9.6–18.4% — not worth taking damage. If Excadrill gets Thunder Waved by Klefki's Prankster priority, its Speed drops to ~140 (still outspeeds Rotom/Klefki but loses to Dragapult 178–213). Plan after KOing Klefki: bring in Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag trapping or Houndoom for Dragapult/Metagross wallbreaking depending on what opponent brings in. Excadrill at 1 HP (if sashed) should be pivoted out immediately. Watch for Rotom Volt Switch pivoting into Incineroar (Intimidate) or Metagross-Mega.

decisions.rationale: Switch Klefki to Incineroar to trigger Intimidate, weakening both foes' Attack stacks with burn on Tyranitar. Incineroar survives any unboosted hit comfortably through Reflect, and even Helping Hand + High Horsepower is only a roll to OHKO (82–117%). Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump guarantees the KO on 1% Excadrill if it connects (80% accurate), removing the fastest threat. Klefki is preserved for potential Light Screen later.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, burned) + Excadrill (Focus Sash consumed, Sand Rush) and two of Gengar-Mega, Houndoom, Gholdengo, Tauros-Aqua. Rotom-Wash walls Excadrill with Levitate. Klefki's Prankster fails against Dark-type targets (Tyranitar); Thunder Wave also fails vs Ground (Excadrill). Burn on Tyranitar cuts its physical damage. Excadrill's Protect success rate is reduced after turn 2 use. Incineroar's Intimidate further cripples Tyranitar's physical output.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Klefki with Tyranitar Crunch and Excadrill Iron Head — both guaranteed KO at 4% even through Reflect/burn. This ensures Klefki dies regardless of Prankster Thunder Wave paralysis on Excadrill. Excadrill at 1 HP is expected to fall to Rotom Hydro Pump after completing its job. Keeping Gengar on the bench preserves it at 100% for a clean switch-in next turn to Mega Evolve with Shadow Tag, avoiding the 65.7–97.1% Hydro Pump risk if it switched in this turn.
decisions.notebook: Tyranitar Crunch guaranteed KOs Klefki at 4% even through Reflect+burn+NVE (6.7–12.9% of max). Excadrill Iron Head also guaranteed KOs Klefki (36.6–68.9%). Rotom Hydro Pump does 65.7–97.1% to Gengar — never switch Gengar into Rotom's predicted Hydro Pump. Plan: after Klefki KO and Excadrill fainting, bring in Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag trapping. Tyranitar burned at 88% is a pivot/sandsetter only. Watch for opponent's 4th mon (Incineroar/Corviknight/Metagross — only one is in this game). Houndoom is the backup wallbreaker for Dragapult/Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Bring in Gengar to Mega Evolve into Gengar-Mega for Shadow Tag, trapping Incineroar and Rotom-Wash and preventing Klefki from switching in for a Prankster Thunder Wave. Gengar-Mega outspeeds both active foes (165-200 vs 80-112 and 106-138) and has Energy Ball SE on Rotom-Wash. Tyranitar stays as burned sand-setting pivot. This matches the pre-game plan of Shadow Tag trapping after Klefki neutralization.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega (Timid, Gengarite) reaches 165-200 Speed with Shadow Tag — traps all non-Ghost types. Dragapult (Ghost) is immune to Shadow Tag and outspeeds at 178-213, so it remains the priority threat; Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball is SE on Dragapult. Houndoom (Timid, Life Orb, Flash Fire, Speed 161) is the backup wallbreaker for Dragapult/Metagross and has Sucker Punch priority. Opponent brought Dragapult/Klefki/Incineroar/Rotom-Wash this game (Corviknight and Metagross not brought). Klefki is Steel-type so immune to sandstorm damage. Incineroar Fake Out fails after its first turn on field (entered turn 4, so fails from turn 5 onward).

decisions.rationale: Rotom is at 52% and Gengar-Mega outspeeds and threatens an Energy Ball OHKO range (51–73.9%). Protect keeps Rotom safe. Incineroar's Darkest Lariat into Gengar has a strong OHKO chance (69.5–146.7%) and at worst leaves Gengar in easy cleanup range. Tyranitar is burned, -1 Atk, and its free turn is low-impact (Rock Slide 10–14% on Incineroar through Reflect). This preserves both my Pokémon while heavily pressuring the opponent's Mega.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, burned, -1 Atk) + Excadrill (fainted) + Gengar-Mega. Fourth unrevealed among Houndoom, Gholdengo, Tauros-Aqua. Klefki at 5% is fragile; Dragapult is threatened by Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball (87–125% OHKO range). Incineroar's Darkest Lariat is my best Gengar answer. Rotom-Wash must avoid Energy Ball KOs.

decisions.rationale: Double Protect + Mega Evolve safely establishes Shadow Tag, trapping both foes (no switches, no Volt Switch escape). Sandstorm chips Rotom-Wash from 51% to ~45%, below Energy Ball's 49.7% minimum damage — guaranteeing a KO next turn WITHOUT Helping Hand, so Tyranitar can Protect too. This avoids the catastrophic risk of going aggressive now: if the opponent Protects Rotom-Wash and Darkest Lariats Gengar (guaranteed OHKO at 119.7-175.2%), we'd lose Gengar for nothing and face a 2v4. By waiting one turn, we gain Shadow Tag control, sandstorm chip, and information on opponent targeting, while preserving both Pokémon at full health. Next turn: Tyranitar Protect + Gengar-Mega Energy Ball on Rotom-Wash for guaranteed KO, with Tyranitar safe from retaliation.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag traps all non-Ghost types; Dragapult (Ghost) immune. Incineroar Darkest Lariat OHKOs Gengar (119.7-175.2%) — must Protect Gengar or switch to Houndoom when Incineroar threatens. Energy Ball on Rotom-Wash: 49.7-92.8% min without Helping Hand, 73.9-139.2% with Helping Hand (guaranteed KO). After 1 turn sandstorm chip (~6.25%), Rotom at ~45% is below Energy Ball's 49.7% minimum — guaranteed KO without Helping Hand. Houndoom (Dark/Fire, Flash Fire, Life Orb, Speed 161) walls Incineroar (Flare Blitz immune, Darkest Lariat NVE) and threatens Dragapult with Sucker Punch (SE priority). Klefki at 4% is a free KO. Opponent brought Dragapult/Klefki/Incineroar/Rotom-Wash; Corviknight and Metagross not brought.

decisions.rationale: Rotom faces a likely Helping Hand + Energy Ball from Gengar-Mega that guarantees a KO if it stays in. Switching to Dragapult absorbs Energy Ball comfortably (20-28% unboosted, 31-43% with Helping Hand) while Incineroar's Darkest Lariat has a ~41% chance to OHKO Gengar-Mega outright and severely weakens it otherwise. The opponent must predict the switch with Shadow Ball to punish, but the straightforward play of targeting the threatened Rotom with Energy Ball is more probable. Preserving Rotom for later is crucial.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, burned, -1 Atk) + Excadrill (fainted) + Gengar-Mega. Fourth unrevealed among Houndoom, Gholdengo, Tauros-Aqua. Klefki at 5% dies to sand on switch-in. Dragapult is OHKO'd by Gengar Shadow Ball but tanks Energy Ball. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is my primary Gengar answer (61-117%). Rotom-Wash must avoid Gengar Energy Ball.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is trapped by Shadow Tag and cannot switch. Gengar threatens Rotom-Wash with Energy Ball (65-90% through Reflect, possible KO). The best counterplay is to double-target Gengar: Darkest Lariat (61-117%) plus Hydro Pump (43-82%) gives a high probability of KOing Gengar before it can claim a second KO. Even if Rotom-Wash falls to Energy Ball first, Darkest Lariat alone has a solid roll to remove Gengar, leaving burned -1 Tyranitar vs Incineroar in a favorable endgame.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, burned, -1 Atk) + Excadrill (fainted) + Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag, traps non-Ghosts). Fourth unrevealed among Houndoom, Gholdengo, Tauros-Aqua. Klefki at 5% dies to sand on switch-in. Dragapult is OHKO'd by Gengar Shadow Ball but tanks Energy Ball. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is my primary Gengar answer (61-117%). Rotom-Wash must avoid Gengar Energy Ball. Shadow Tag confirmed: non-Ghost active Pokémon cannot switch.

decisions.rationale: Switch Gengar-Mega to Houndoom to dodge Incineroar's guaranteed-OHKO Darkest Lariat (causing it to whiff), bringing in a fresh Houndoom that walls Incineroar (Flash Fire + Dark resist) and outspeeds both active foes. Gengar-Mega is preserved at 94% on bench—Mega Evolution persists through switching, so Shadow Tag returns when re-brought. Tyranitar uses Rock Slide to chip both foes (survives even a double-target: Darkest Lariat 11-16% + Hydro Pump 36-55% = 47-71%, Tyranitar at 77% lives). This keeps 3 Pokémon alive with Shadow Tag available later, far superior to trading Gengar for Rotom and losing Shadow Tag permanently.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega retains Mega form when switched out (Gen7 mechanic); can re-enter with Shadow Tag later. Houndoom (Dark/Fire, Flash Fire, Life Orb, Speed 161, Timid) walls Incineroar completely (Flare Blitz immune, Darkest Lariat NVE 0.5x) and outspeeds both Incineroar (80-112) and Rotom-Wash (106-138). Houndoom Sucker Punch is SE priority on Dragapult (Ghost). Tyranitar burned + atk-1 makes its physical attacks very weak (Rock Slide 8-14% on Incineroar, 5-8% on Rotom). Klefki at 4% is Steel-type (immune to sandstorm chip) but dies to any hit. Opponent has Reflect (5 turns) reducing physical damage. Dragapult (178-213 Speed) may outspeed Gengar-Mega (200); Dragapult is Ghost-type so immune to Shadow Tag. Game 1 plan: preserve Gengar-Mega for late-game Shadow Tag control; use Houndoom to handle Incineroar and pressure Dragapult with Sucker Punch.

decisions.rationale: Rotom Hydro Pump into Houndoom has a 90.1–169.3% range, likely KOing the biggest offensive threat. Incineroar Protect keeps it safe from the turn's damage. Houndoom is faster than Rotom, but without Helping Hand its Dark Pulse (39.5–57.3%) plus Tyranitar Rock Slide (5.1–7.6%) leaves Rotom a solid chance to survive and fire back. If the opponent uses Helping Hand, Rotom may still barely live a low roll. Incineroar's own attacks are all NVE or immune into both foes, so Protect extracts maximum value.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, burned, -1 Atk) + Excadrill (fainted) + Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag, traps non-Ghosts when active) + Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire). Klefki at 5% dies to sand on switch-in. Dragapult Shadow Ball is SE on Gengar-Mega; Dragapult is OHKO'd by Gengar Shadow Ball but tanks Energy Ball. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is my primary Gengar answer. Rotom-Wash must avoid Gengar Energy Ball. Shadow Tag only active when Gengar-Mega is on field.

decisions.rationale: Switch Tyranitar to Gengar-Mega to activate Shadow Tag, trapping both Incineroar and Rotom-Wash (neither is Ghost-type). Houndoom Protects to avoid the guaranteed-KO Hydro Pump from Rotom-Wash. Any opponent move targeting Tyranitar's slot fails (switched out), and moves targeting Houndoom are blocked by Protect. Next turn: Gengar-Mega Energy Ball is a guaranteed KO on Rotom-Wash (61.1-113.6% from 59% HP), and the opponent remains trapped by Shadow Tag. This preserves both Pokémon at high HP while gaining massive positional advantage.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega retains Mega form when switched out (Gen7); Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost types. Gengar-Mega Energy Ball is guaranteed KO on Rotom-Wash from 59%. Houndoom Sucker Punch is SE priority on Dragapult (Ghost). Tyranitar burned + atk-1 makes physical attacks negligible; preserve for late-game sand reset if needed. Opponent Klefki at 4% is Steel (sand-immune) but dies to any hit; watch for Prankster Thunder Wave. Dragapult (178-213 Speed) may outspeed Gengar-Mega (200) and is Ghost (immune to Shadow Tag). Game 1 plan: trap with Shadow Tag, KO Rotom-Wash with Energy Ball, then clean up Incineroar/Klefki, save Houndoom Sucker Punch for Dragapult.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is trapped by Shadow Tag and outsped by Gengar-Mega, whose Energy Ball is a guaranteed OHKO from 54%. Rotom must Protect to survive. Incineroar's Darkest Lariat has a roll to OHKO Gengar-Mega (61–117%); even if it misses the KO, Gengar is heavily damaged. Houndoom cannot KO Incineroar this turn even with both foes targeting it (max ~31% combined). If Gengar falls, Shadow Tag lifts and I can bring Dragapult freely next turn. Incineroar's Protect is unreliable at 1/3 consecutive success, so attacking is higher value.

Gengar Energy Ball guaranteed KOs Rotom-Wash (53% HP, KO from 59%), removing the only SE threat to Houndoom. Houndoom Dark Pulse on Incineroar chips 15-28% and carries 20% flinch chance since Houndoom (161) outspeeds Incineroar (80-112) — the sole way to potentially save Gengar from guaranteed-KO Darkest Lariat while still eliminating Rotom. If Gengar dies, the trade is favorable: Houndoom + Tyranitar vs weakened Incineroar + 4% Klefki + Dragapult, with Houndoom Sucker Punch (29-54% SE priority) as the Dragapult answer.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega retains Mega form when switched out (Gen7); Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost types. Gengar-Mega Energy Ball guaranteed KO on Rotom-Wash from 59%. Incineroar Darkest Lariat guaranteed KO on Gengar-Mega from 88% (SE Dark vs Ghost). Houndoom Sucker Punch does 29-54% to Dragapult (SE priority, not KO from 93%). All Dragapult moves (Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Fire Blast) are neutral or NVE on Houndoom (Dark/Fire + Flash Fire). Houndoom Dark Pulse flinch chance (20%) is live when Houndoom outspeeds target. Tyranitar burned + atk-1 makes physical attacks negligible; preserve for late-game sand reset. Opponent Klefki at 4% is Steel (sand-immune) but dies to any hit; watch for Prankster Thunder Wave. Game 1 plan: trap with Shadow Tag, KO Rotom-Wash with Energy Ball, then clean up Incineroar/Klefki, save Houndoom Sucker Punch for Dragapult.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Houndoom is the only opposing threat that can KO Rotom-Wash before it moves (Dark Pulse 39.5–57.3% into 54% HP). Hydro Pump OHKOs Houndoom (90.1–169.3%). Incineroar's Darkest Lariat adds chip insurance against an 80% Hydro Pump miss and does 18.1–37.3% if Rotom goes down. Tyranitar is burned, -1 Atk, and its Rock Slide does only 14.9–21.3% to Incineroar and 8.3–11.5% to Rotom; once Houndoom falls, Tyranitar alone cannot sweep. Accepting the risk that Helping Hand + Dark Pulse always KOs Rotom, doubling Houndoom is the highest-EV path to a 2v1 endgame.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, burned, -1 Atk) + Excadrill (fainted) + Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) + Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire). Klefki at 5% faints to nearly any hit. Dragapult is OHKO'd by Houndoom Dark Pulse. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump is my only guaranteed OHKO on Houndoom. Incineroar cannot use Fake Out (not first turn on field). Both of my remaining backline mons are fragile; preserving Rotom-Wash is critical to winning.

decisions.rationale: Klefki can set Light Screen with Prankster priority before being KO'd. Light Screen targets our side, bypassing Dark-type Prankster immunity. With both screens up, Dragapult survives Houndoom's Dark Pulse on turn 11 and the game becomes winnable. Sending Dragapult now risks an immediate OHKO from Dark Pulse before it can contribute. Forfeiting is premature; the position is difficult but winnable with screen support.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, burned, -1 Atk) + Excadrill (fainted) + Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag, fainted) + Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire). Klefki at 5% faints to nearly any hit but can set Light Screen before dying. Dragapult is OHKO'd by Houndoom Dark Pulse without Light Screen. Both opponents are Dark-type, making Prankster status moves fail against them, but field-targeting screens work. Win condition: set both screens, preserve Dragapult, eliminate Houndoom first.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand (priority +5) boosts Houndoom's Dark Pulse to a guaranteed KO on Rotom-Wash (57-107% from 53%), and Houndoom outspeeds Rotom-Wash (161 vs 106-138) so it lands before Rotom can Hydro Pump (which would guaranteed KO Houndoom). Tyranitar survives even if Rotom Protects (~11%) and Hydro Pumps it (max 55% from 71%). Incineroar's attacks are all NVE/immune on both my mons. Eliminating Rotom-Wash preserves the 2v1 advantage.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega retains Mega form when switched out (Gen7); Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost types. Houndoom Dark Pulse + Helping Hand guaranteed KOs Rotom-Wash from 53%. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump guaranteed KOs Houndoom from 78% and does 36-55% to Tyranitar. Tyranitar burned + Intimidate makes Rock Slide only 11-21% to Incineroar (cannot KO from 24%). Houndoom outspeeds Rotom-Wash (161 vs 106-138) but is outspeed by Dragapult (178-213). Houndoom Sucker Punch does 29-54% to Dragapult (not KO from 93%). All Dragapult moves neutral/NVE on Houndoom. Incineroar Darkest Lariat NVE on both Tyranitar and Houndoom. Rotom-Wash Protect at reduced success rate after 2 uses (~11%). Klefki at 4% dies to any hit; watch for Prankster Thunder Wave. Late-game plan: preserve Houndoom Sucker Punch for Dragapult, use Tyranitar for sand reset and Helping Hand support.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Incineroar)
decisions.rationale: Klefki's Prankster Light Screen goes up at +1 priority before any foe attack, halving special damage for 8 turns (Light Clay). Incineroar Protects to guarantee survival through the turn, blocking Tyranitar Rock Slide and any Houndoom attack aimed its way. Houndoom's Flamethrower KOs Klefki regardless, but Light Screen is already set. Next turn Dragapult replaces Klefki, giving us Incineroar + Dragapult vs both foes under Light Screen, where Dragapult outspeeds and Thunderbolt has ~88% chance to KO Houndoom. This is safer than gambling on a ~33% Darkest Lariat KO now while risking Incineroar fainting to Rock Slide.

If opponent switches Incineroar out for Dragapult, Helping Hand-boosted Flamethrower hits Dragapult neutrally for ~47-90% — a huge chunk. If they switch Klefki for Dragapult, Flamethrower still KOs Incineroar and we face Dragapult 2v1 with Sucker Punch ready.

decisions.rationale: Houndoom at 9% with Life Orb: any damaging attack it makes will cause 10% recoil and self-KO. It must Protect to survive. decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult is the sole win condition. Houndoom at 9% with Life Orb self-KOs on any attack (recoil > remaining HP). Opponent's only viable Houndoom play is Protect. decisions.rationale: Helping Hand boosts Houndoom's unrevealed Sucker Punch to 42.6-79.8% of Dragapult's max HP. Houndoom faints from its own Life Orb but the trade is decisive — Tyranitar then cleans up Klefki (4%) and Incineroar (12%) with Rock Slide. Opponent has no reason to expect Sucker Punch (unrevealed), making Dragapult attacking the most likely outcome.
decisions.notebook: Houndoom Sucker Punch is unrevealed to opponent — key endgame tool. Helping Hand + Sucker Punch does 42.6-79.8% to Dragapult (guaranteed KO from 48% via direct damage or Life Orb recoil). Without Helping Hand, Sucker Punch does 29.2-54% (only 24% direct KO from 48%). Tyranitar Crunch does 19-36.2% to Dragapult (burned, SE). Rock Slide does 6.7-12.3% to Dragapult (neutral, spread). Dragapult Thunderbolt does 11.1-17.4% to Tyranitar. Rock Slide KOs both Klefki (4%) and Incineroar (12%) even when burned+Intimidated. Opponent bench: Incineroar 12%, Corviknight and Metagross (Metagrossite) not brought in game 1.

decisions.rationale: Prankster Thunder Wave fails on Dark-type Tyranitar, so Klefki must attack. Thunderbolt (14-24%) + Foul Play (8.2-17.1%) leaves Tyranitar at 5.9-24.8%. Tyranitar's only threatening move is Crunch on Dragapult (30.3-42.4% through Reflect), but only the absolute max roll KOs Dragapult from 42% — roughly a 1/16 chance. Even if Dragapult falls, Incineroar cleans up the weakened Tyranitar. This line maximizes damage while accepting minimal risk.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Prankster status moves (Thunder Wave) fail against Dark-type Tyranitar. Dragapult is the sole win condition; its Thunderbolt is the best damage into Tyranitar. Incineroar has unused Fake Out and can Intimidate again if needed. Klefki at 5% is immune to Sandstorm (Steel type).

decisions.rationale: Rock Slide is the only play that can remove Klefki (4% HP) and its Prankster Thunder Wave threat this turn. Damage range 3-6.1% vs 4% HP isn't a guaranteed KO between accuracy and rolls, but ~61% to kill Klefki is far better than letting it freely Thunder Wave me next turn. If Klefki faints, Incineroar (12%) enters and becomes the next Rock Slide target. Crunch Dragapult chips it to ~6-23% but guarantees Klefki Thunder Waves me, which effectively ends the game. Playing for the small chance to win game 1 rather than forfeiting, since I already have full info on opponent's sets for games 2-3.

(3) Klefki Prankster screens + Thunder Wave are oppressive; Taunt from Gengar-Mega can shut this down if positioned well. (4) Incineroar Chople Berry + Intimidate means it survives one SE hit and weakens physical attackers — plan around it. (5) Dragapult Protect usage (2 times) means it's less likely to Protect again.

reflections.summary: Incineroar's Darkest Lariat OHKOed Mega Gengar on turn 8, removing the opponent's fastest special threat. Klefki's Light Screen and Reflect coupled with the early burn on Tyranitar allowed the team to weather subsequent attacks, and Dragapult closed out the game with Thunderbolt as the remaining special win condition.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, anticipate more cautious play around Mega Gengar—protects or switches—and a possible shift to the Gholdengo/Tauros-Aqua core. Consider leading with Incineroar and Klefki to apply Fake Out pressure and set screens early, while preserving Dragapult in the back to handle Tyranitar and potential Gholdengo.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's sand mode: Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Helping Hand, Careful) paired with Excadrill (Focus Sash, Adamant) or Houndoom (Life Orb, Sucker Punch, Flash Fire). Tyranitar often uses Helping Hand to boost Houndoom's Dark Pulse or Flamethrower. Mega Gengar is frail and may be protected more carefully or replaced by Gholdengo (Leftovers, Recover, Dazzling Gleam) or Tauros-Aqua (Intimidate, Wave Crash, Sitrus Berry) in game 2. Opponent's Helping Hand + Sucker Punch gambits can be exploited with Protect. Incineroar's Darkest Lariat remains key for pressuring Ghost-types; preserve it for Gengar or Gholdengo. Screens from Klefki are critical to mitigate spread damage; protect Klefki early. Dragapult's special movepool is the primary win condition but must be wary of Flash Fire if Houndoom returns.

reflections.summary: Lost because Tyranitar was burned by Rotom-Wash Will-O-Wisp on turn 2, crippling physical damage for the entire game, while Excadrill fell to back-to-back Hydro Pumps by turn 4. With the sand-rush sweeper gone and Tyranitar weakened, Klefki's screens stalled out remaining damage, and Gengar-Mega was caught by Incineroar Darkest Lariat without Protect on turn 8. Houndoom's Sucker Punch failed into Dragapult Protect on turn 12, sealing the loss.
reflections.adjustment: Lead Gengar-Mega + Houndoom or Gengar-Mega + Excadrill to Taunt Klefki's screens early and avoid feeding Tyranitar to Rotom-Wash Will-O-Wisp. Houndoom's Flash Fire makes it immune to Will-O-Wisp, so use it as the Rotom-Wash switch-in instead of Tyranitar. Preserve Gengar-Mega Protect for Incineroar's Darkest Lariat timing rather than spending it on predicted Rotom Protect.
